old: On a museum visit, 35 students could see the science gallery, the art gallery, both or neither. 28 students saw the science gallery and 25 saw the art gallery. What is the least possible number of students who saw both galleries?
new: On a museum visit, each of 35 students saw the science gallery, the art gallery, both or neither. Of them, 28 saw the science gallery and 25 saw the art gallery. What is the least possible number of students who saw both galleries?
why: 'could see' is vague (allowed vs did see); second sentence starts with a numeral.

old: At most 35 students saw at least one gallery, so at least 28 + 25 − 35 = 18 saw both. 18 is possible when every student saw a gallery.
new: At most 35 students saw at least one gallery, so at least 28 + 25 − 35 = 18 saw both. This is possible when every student saw a gallery.
